post_title: How many new locally acquired dengue cases will the Week 42 FDOH arbovirus report (October 18–24, 2026) show for Florida?

question.title: How many new locally acquired dengue cases will the Week 42 FDOH arbovirus report (October 18–24, 2026) show for Florida?
question.description:
The Florida Department of Health (FDOH) publishes a Weekly Arbovirus Surveillance Report tracking mosquito-borne diseases including dengue. Each report has a "Dengue Cases Acquired in Florida" section stating how many locally acquired dengue cases were "reported this week" and the cumulative total for the year. Reports are posted roughly one week after the epidemiological week ends (the Week 40 report covering Oct 4–10 was published Oct 15, 2026).

In 2026 Florida has experienced an unusually large local dengue outbreak, concentrated heavily in Hillsborough County (Tampa Bay area). Weekly new locally acquired case counts reported recently were: Week 34 (ending ~Sep 3): 32; Week 35: 38; Week 36: 41; and the trend continued upward through autumn, with 62 new cases in the Week 38 report and 72 new cases in the Week 40 report (Oct 4–10), bringing the cumulative 2026 total to 368 locally acquired cases across eight counties. Intensive aerial and ground mosquito spraying has been underway in Hillsborough, Pinellas, Pasco and neighboring counties. Florida's mosquito season typically winds down heading into late October and November, which could slow transmission, while surveillance and testing backlogs can also shift when cases appear in a given week's report.

Week 42 covers October 18–24, 2026, and its report is expected around October 29, 2026.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number of locally acquired dengue cases reported "this week" in the Florida Department of Health Weekly Arbovirus Surveillance Report for Week 42 of 2026 (covering the epidemiological week of October 18–24, 2026), expected to be published on or around October 29, 2026. The report is accessible from the FDOH Arbovirus Surveillance page (https://www.floridahealth.gov/statistics-data/population-surveillance/arbovirus-surveillance/), and the Week 42 PDF is expected at a URL of the form https://www.floridahealth.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/fl-arbovirus-report-w42-2026.pdf. The resolution value is the count stated in the "Dengue Cases Acquired in Florida" section as the number of locally acquired dengue cases "reported this week" (e.g., the Week 40 report stated "Seventy-two cases of locally acquired dengue were reported this week," which would resolve as 72).
question.fine_print: If the Week 42 report is published later than expected, resolution waits for it. If FDOH restructures the report so that no single weekly ("this week") locally acquired dengue count is stated, the weekly value will be computed as the increase in the cumulative 2026 locally acquired dengue total from the immediately preceding published report to the Week 42 report. If the report is permanently unavailable and the figure cannot be recovered from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), the question is annulled.
